learnings.question: Economist Herbert Simon warned about the growing scarcity of human attention in an information-rich world all the way back in which decade?
learnings.learning: Herbert Simon observed in 1971 that an information-rich world creates a scarcity of attention, since information consumes the attention of those who receive it — a warning that predates the internet by decades.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: In a daily automated content-curation system built to filter YouTube recommendations, what single qualifying question does the AI ask about each video before deciding whether to keep it?
options: Would this video go viral on social media?
Is this video under 20 minutes long?
Does this video contain any sponsored content?
Would a Muslim, Malaysian software engineer early in his career actually benefit from watching this?
learnings.learning: A personal content engine runs a script daily that pulls new videos from trusted channels and filters them with a single targeted question about whether they'd benefit a specific kind of viewer, discarding anything that doesn't pass.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: Which 19th-century psychologist demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned information within 24 hours unless they actively work to recall it?
learnings.learning: Back in the 1880s, Hermann Ebbinghaus proved that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively force themselves to recall it, which is why re-reading notes doesn't work as well as being quizzed on them.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What term do researchers use to describe the tendency for our brains to stop retaining information once we know it's been saved somewhere else, like a phone or a notebook?
learnings.learning: Researchers behind the 'Google Effect' paper call this phenomenon Digital Amnesia: the moment we write something down or store it digitally, our brains treat that as permission to let it go.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, which artifact visually tracks the amount of work remaining in a Sprint to help a team see if it's on schedule?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is one of Scrum's three key artifacts, visualizing the progress of a Sprint and showing the remaining work so a team can track whether it's on schedule.

learnings.question: Which of these roles is commonly mistaken for being part of the Scrum framework, even though it is NOT one of the three official Scrum roles?
learnings.learning: Scrum defines exactly three roles — Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developers — and a 'Project Manager' is not one of them, despite being a common assumption from traditional project management.

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what Arabic term describes humanity's role as caretakers or stewards of the Earth, responsible for preserving faith and fostering unity?
learnings.learning: Khalifah is the term for humanity's role as stewards or caretakers of the Earth, a responsibility that goes beyond personal conduct to preserving the faith and unity of the community.

learnings.question: In the Quran, what reason does Allah give for having created jinn and mankind?
learnings.learning: Quran 51:56 states that jinn and mankind were created for the specific purpose of worshiping Allah, which forms the foundational purpose of life in Islamic theology.

learnings.question: In Islamic teaching about the purpose of life, which three primary roles are humans said to fulfill?
options: Working, raising a family, and worshiping Allah
Serving the community, pursuing a career, and seeking wealth
Worship, stewardship of the Earth, and accountability in the Hereafter
learnings.learning: Life's purpose in Islam revolves around three primary roles: worshiping Allah, serving as stewards (khalifah) of the Earth, and preparing for the Hereafter through conscious, accountable choices.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which low-power link state is described as a 'very light sleep,' designed for only very short idle durations and able to wake up quickly?
learnings.learning: L0s is a very light sleep state in PCIe power management, meant for short durations of idleness, letting the link quickly wake up to resume full activity.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Which PCIe power state is comparable to a computer being completely shut down, offering the greatest power savings but requiring the longest time to restart?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power state, comparable to a computer being completely shut down — it minimizes power use the most but takes the longest to restart.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what term refers to the actual unfolding of events in a person's life, as shaped by their actions and decisions — distinct from Allah's eternal, preordained plan?
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual occurrence of events in life as they unfold, shaped by a person's own actions and decisions, as distinct from Qadr, which is Allah's complete, eternal plan.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: According to Surah Ar-Ra'd (13:11), Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what?
learnings.learning: Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:11 teaches that Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves, framing personal change as a precondition for a changed outcome.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: In Arabic script, what term describes the small diacritical markings placed above or below letters to indicate vowel sounds and pronunciation?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are small markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds; without them, the same letters can be read multiple ways, which is why their omission adds ambiguity.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: A data analysis applying the Pareto Principle (the 80/20 rule) to the Quran's text found that its 20 most frequently used words account for roughly what percentage of the entire text?
learnings.learning: Unlike the classic 80/20 Pareto split, the top 20 most frequent words in the Quran only accumulate to about 20.83% of its total text, even though they're still worth mastering first.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
